**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-190704, Reactome:R-HSA-190827, Reactome:R-HSA-190861, Reactome:R-HSA-190872)

**Proposed mechanism:** GJB2 variant in KIHI (MONDO:0007850) —DISRUPTS→ GJB2 (HGNC:4284); GJB2 (HGNC:4284) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction communication in cochlear supporting cells (GO:0005934); Gap junction communication in cochlear supporting cells (GO:0005934) —LEADS_TO→ Inner ear homeostasis disruption (HP:0000377); GJB2 variant in NSHL (MONDO:0019497) —DISRUPTS→ GJB2 (HGNC:4284); GJB2 (HGNC:4284) —DISRUPTS→ Keratinocyte differentiation (GO:0048066); Keratinocyte differentiation (GO:0048066) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermal barrier dysfunction (HP:0001064); Inner ear homeostasis disruption (HP:0000377) —LEADS_TO→ connextin26; connextin26 —LEADS_TO→ GJB2 variant in NSHL (MONDO:0019497); Epidermal barrier dysfunction (HP:0001064) —LEADS_TO→ GJB2 variant in KIHI (MONDO:0007850). Mutations in GJB2 disrupt gap junction communication in the inner ear, leading to hearing loss (nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss), and also affect keratinocyte differentiation and epidermal barrier function, contributing to the ichthyosis and keratitis seen in KIHS.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in GJB2 associated with KIHS that do not show any reduced penetrance or association with hearing loss in large population databases like gnomAD. _(variant: ExAC:1331323)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting GJB2 function or downstream pathways could offer therapeutic strategies for both hearing loss and skin manifestations, though the specific therapeutic approach might need to account for the different phenotypic outcomes.
